title: Invoice timestamp watermarking and backfill safety for delayed metering events
creator: Maya Chen
description: Address invoice mismatches caused by delayed usage events that arrive after export windows. Implement deterministic export signature and per-customer watermarking to prevent duplicate adjustment lines in NetSuite/Stripe and improve reconciliation idempotency.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Observed recurring invoice mismatches when delayed usage events arrive after hourly export window. Stakeholders: finance, revenue operations. Initial hypothesis: late arrival combined with current export windowing leads to duplicate adjustment lines in NetSuite and Stripe proration mismatches.

2026-03-03 - Investigation: Reproduced locally with synthetic delayed events. Root cause: exporter anchors to hour boundary using event ingestion timestamp rather than canonical processing watermark. When delayed events are backfilled they get assigned to previous windows but reconciliation deduplicator relies on export idempotency that uses ingestion timestamp -> second line created.

2026-03-05 - Design decision: Implement watermarking per-customer that tracks last-exported-event-time and uses event.original_timestamp if older than watermark for attribution; also introduce deterministic export signature including watermark and exporter-version. Proposed two-step migration: 1) Safe-mode exports adding new signature as metadata while preserving old lines; 2) Cutover where reconciliation prefers new signature and marks legacy lines as superseded.

2026-03-07 - Implementation notes: Added per-customer watermark in billing DB (nullable timestamp). Exporter now computes signed_export_id = sha256(customer_id + export_window_start + watermark_iso + exporter_version). Added feature flag billing/watermarked-exports for staged rollout. See RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/watermarks-2026 (internal).

2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4827 - exporter changes + schema migration. Includes migration to backfill watermark=null for customers with no outstanding late events and a dry-run mode to produce 'watermarked_signature' column without writing to Stripe/NetSuite.

2026-03-09 - QA: Ran dry-run against a copy of last month's exports. Found one edge-case where multi-tenant events crossing DST boundary produced mismatched windows — fixed by normalizing to UTC before computing watermark. Also added unit tests for deterministic signature generation.

2026-03-10 - Rollout plan: Start with 5% of exports (non-revenue critical customers) for 48 hours; monitor billing-export-anomalies dashboard and NetSuite reconciliation queue for duplicate lines. If stable, increase to 25% then 100% over 72 hours. Rollback: disable feature flag and run reconciliation job to map new signatures to legacy-lines for customers impacted.

2026-03-10 - Open items: 1) Create migration job to backfill watermark for customers with known late-arrival histories; 2) Update finance-runbooks to understand new 'watermarked_signature' field in exports CSV; 3) Determine whether to backfill historical invoices or only apply moving forward (finance prefers moving forward unless discrepancies exceed threshold).
notes: Migration will require small schema change: billing.customer_watermark TIMESTAMP NULLABLE; aim to keep migration online via backfill in batches.
Finance to be warned of ~24-48 hour window where both legacy and watermarked signatures might appear; reconciliation tooling will be updated to dedupe by signed_export_id when both present.
release_notes: Fix: Reduce duplicate adjustment lines caused by late-arriving usage events by introducing per-customer watermarking and deterministic export signatures. Staged rollout to limit customer impact and provide rollback path.
